documents.title: Press Release - CPCL Financial Performance For The Quarter And Half Year Ended 30.09.2026

analysis.summary: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported its financial and operational performance for Q4 and full-year FY26, achieving a highest-ever annual crude throughput of 11.71 MMT at 112% capacity utilization. The company reported a full-year GRM of $9.2 per barrel and a Q4 GRM of $13.75 per barrel. CPCL reduced its gross debt to INR 1,900 crores and net debt to INR 973 crores, achieving a gross debt-equity ratio of 0.18. Additionally, the company announced a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year and outlined plans for an INR 2,000 crore capex program covering a Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project and retail outlet expansion over the next 2 to 3 years. Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) reported its Q4 and full-year FY 2024-25 results, achieving an annual crude throughput of 10.45 MMT (99.5% capacity utilization) and Q4 throughput of 2.974 MMT (113% capacity utilization).

guidance.claim: Management expects operational and financial performance momentum to continue into FY27.
guidance.quote: To summarize, we continue to deliver resilient operational and financial performance and see the momentum to continue in the new financial year as well.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects commissioning from its retail outlet licenses to begin in FY27.
guidance.quote: And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

guidance.claim: CPCL expects normal maintenance and regular CAPEX for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
guidance.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

demand_outlook.claim: CPCL achieved record LPG production of 447 TMT to meet domestic requirements during global LPG availability uncertainties.
demand_outlook.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever LPG production of 447 TMT, overcoming previous record of 404 set in 2023-'24. With global uncertainties affecting the availability of LPG all over the world, CPCL is happy to step up the requirement when the nation needed it.

demand_outlook.claim: Motor Spirit (MS) demand in the southern Indian market faces a supply shortfall of around 20 TMT per month.
demand_outlook.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month.

demand_outlook.claim: Southern market demand growth is projected at 4%-5% for MS and 3% for HSD.
demand_outlook.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred a capex of INR 856 crores in FY26 compared to INR 673 crores in FY25.
capex_expansion.quote: During the current year, the capex was INR856 crores as compared to INR673 crores in the previous year.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL plans an INR 1,600 crore Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project and an INR 400 crore retail outlet expansion project over 2 to 3 years alongside normal annual capex of INR 500 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years. Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

capex_expansion.claim: The Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project will add a new capacity of 250 KTPA.
capex_expansion.quote: My new unit will take me to a 250,000, 250 KTPA in Group 2, Group 3 capacity, and that will be a fresh addition.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL doubled its Hexane capacity from 30 to 60.
capex_expansion.quote: It was 30, now the capacity is 60.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL incurred a CAPEX expenditure of Rs. 673 crores during FY 2024-25.
capex_expansion.quote: On the CAPEX front, in the current year, we have spent Rs. 673 crores as CAPEX for the current year.

capex_expansion.claim: The revised capital cost for the Cauvery Basin Refinery project is Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity structure between CPCL and Indian Oil.
capex_expansion.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively.

capex_expansion.claim: CPCL has full custody of 1,200 acres of land for the new refinery project at Cauvery Basin.
capex_expansion.quote: So, about 600 acres, which was already with CPCL and another 600 acres, which was acquired in the process, both is in our possession and the pre-project activities of boundary wall construction, and all those things are almost at a big stage.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL achieved a Q4 FY26 GRM of $13.75 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for quarter 4 was $13.75 barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $8.70 per barrel, which again reiterates that all these efficiencies are constant, continuous and are being sustained over each period.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL's core GRM for Q4 FY26 was $10.3 per barrel.
CPCL recorded a foreign exchange loss of approximately INR 200 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR 350 crores for full-year FY26.
margins_costs.quote: For the quarter, it would be for the quarter, it is approximately INR 200 crores,. And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

margins_costs.claim: Niche products represent 7% to 8% of CPCL's volume and contribute around 15% of its margins.
margins_costs.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a full-year GRM of $4.22 per barrel for FY 2024-25 compared to $8.64 per barrel in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: The GRM for 2024-25 for a full year basis is $4.22 per barrel as compared to the previous year $8.64 per barrel, but if you compare it to Singapore benchmark which was $3.79 per barrel in the current year, we have performed better.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL achieved a Q4 FY25 GRM of $6.22 per barrel compared to $7.7 per barrel in Q4 FY24.
margins_costs.quote: On Quarter 4, our GRM was $6.22 per barrel. Again, if I compare the previous year same quarter, it was $7.7 per barrel, but if I compare it to Singapore benchmark, which was only $3.1 per barrel.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL registered its best Energy Intensity Index figure of 87.4 during FY 2024-25.
margins_costs.quote: The best EII figure of 87.4 has been clocked in the current year, 2024-25.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL recorded an inventory gain of $0.66 per barrel or Rs. 125 crores for Q4 FY25.
margins_costs.quote: Yes, the inventory gain is not very significant for the quarter. It is only $ 0.66 per barrel. And in absolute rupee terms, it is Rs. 125 crores only.

margins_costs.claim: CPCL reported a GRM of $3.40 per barrel for 9M FY 2024-25 compared to $8.64 per barrel in FY 2023-24.
CPCL's net operating expenditure stood at ₹945 crore for 9M FY 2024-25.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT in FY26, operating at 112% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL recorded a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT in Q4 FY26, representing 111% capacity utilization.
orders_capacity.quote: In quarter 4 of the current financial year, CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 2.93 MMT, which is also 111% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved highest-ever production of 5.139 MMT of diesel and 1.318 MMT of petrol in FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL concluded the financial year on a high note, achieving the highest ever production levels of 5.139 MMT for diesel HSD, and 1.318 MMT of petrol that is MS, an impressive testament of the refinery's outstanding operational performance.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL recorded its highest-ever distillate yield of 79.1% during FY26.
orders_capacity.quote: Further, highest ever distillate yield of 79.1%, beating our previous record of 77.6% set in 2019-'20 was also achieved during this year.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT for FY 2024-25, representing 99.5% capacity utilization.
orders_capacity.quote: CPCL achieved a crude throughput of 10.45 MMT, equivalent to 99.5% of our installed capacity and this must be seen with respect to the turnaround that has happened during the year and if you take that into consideration , you will find that this performance is quite comparable to the previous year's performance where CPCL clocked 111% capacity utilization and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: Q4 FY25 crude throughput reached 2.974 MMT, equivalent to 113% of installed capacity.
orders_capacity.quote: and coming on to Quarter 4, the crude throughput was 2.974, which is 113% of installed capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed 64% to 65% high sulfur crude during the financial year.
orders_capacity.quote: During the financial year, we have processed almost 64% - 65% of high sulfur.

orders_capacity.claim: CPCL processed crude throughput of 7,480 TMT during 9M FY 2024-25.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL reduced its gross debt-equity ratio to 0.18 from 0.39 in the previous year.
capital_allocation.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's gross borrowings stood at INR 1,900 crores and net borrowings stood at INR 973 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's debt to equity ratio stood at 0.39 as of March 31, 2025, with absolute debt of Rs. 3,100 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: When I turn to leverage position, the debt equity position as on March 31, 2025, is 0.39 compared to 0.32 in the previous year. At an absolute level, the debt stands at Rs. 3,100 crores as compared to Rs. 2,762 crores as on March 31, 2024.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's net worth stood at Rs. 7,939 crores as of March 31, 2025.
capital_allocation.quote: Net worth is at Rs. 7,939 crores as on March 31, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share for FY 2024-25.
capital_allocation.quote: With the above, the Board has also recommended a dividend of Rs. 5 per equity share that is 50% of face value for the current year and as we all know, this is subject to approval at AGM, which will happen in the due course.

capital_allocation.claim: CPCL's net worth stood at ₹7,491 crore as of December 2024 compared to ₹8,593 crore in March 2024.

risks_headwinds.claim: Management highlighted logistical constraints and crude oil price volatility as ongoing business uncertainties.
risks_headwinds.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL experienced a temporary 30% to 40% disruption in Middle East crude supply over a short period.
risks_headwinds.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

risks_headwinds.claim: Uncertainties due to crude price volatility pose ongoing operational challenges.
risks_headwinds.quote: Finally, the uncertainties due to volatility of crude prices do pose a challenge.

risks_headwinds.claim: CPCL incurred a Profit Before Tax loss of ₹374 crore in 9M FY 2024-25.
CPCL incurred an exchange variation loss of ₹122 crore during 9M FY 2024-25.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects to see significant commissioning from its 300 retail outlet licenses during FY26-27.
management_commitments.quote: And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL will deploy INR 2,000 crores over 2 to 3 years toward its Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project and retail expansion.
management_commitments.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL expects normal maintenance and regular CAPEX for the next two years to be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores per year.
management_commitments.quote: The normal maintenance CAPEX for the next two years would be around Rs. 250 to Rs. 300 crores, maintenance CAPEX plus small regular CAPEX normally.

management_commitments.claim: CPCL is planning to use a 2:1 debt to equity ratio for the Nagapattinam refinery joint venture.
management_commitments.quote: Presently, we are working with a 2:1 debt equity for this JV.

management_commitments.claim: One crude unit and the lubes block will undergo scheduled maintenance in FY 2025-26.
management_commitments.quote: In the current financial year 2025-26, one of the other crude units will go for maintenance along with the lubes block as such.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
